items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: Stanley Dance had told Mercer, 'Man, you’ve got to find a clarinet player...'

ctx.x: Those are fairly coveted gigs, aren’t they?

Yup. Absolutely. And “Sophisticated Ladies” was the Broadway show. And that came about because of the fact that I had been out — I had been out on the road — right after Duke died I went out with the band for about [gap] months or whatever. But the reason I went out with the band was because Stanley Dance had told Mercer, “Man, you’ve got to find a clarinet player, because the clarinet is a very important voice in Ellingtonia.” And actually it was Jimmy Hamilton had recommended or suggested that I get the gig…
Those are great — stability and creativity — I think that’s very important for musicians to have a balance there because if they only have stability they’ll be one of those grumpy people who just —
